classification.difficultyReason: Use translations and substitution to sketch six upright parabolas with labelled vertices and y-intercepts.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of the following, labelling the $y$-intercept and vertex.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ five units right. The vertex is $(5,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=5$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-5)^2\\y&=25\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,25)$, symmetric about $x=5$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with labelled y-intercept and vertex; no numerical grid is supplied or required.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=x^2$ one unit right and three units down. The vertex is $(1,-3)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-1)^2-3\\y&=1-3\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,-2)$, symmetric about $x=1$.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with labelled y-intercept and vertex.

Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(0,7)$, symmetric about $x=-2$. It lies above the $x$-axis.
